title: Parsing vs Validation
learningObjectives: Explain the key ideas and terminology of parsing vs validation.
Recognize how the concept is used in real software communication.
Identify common mistakes or risks associated with this topic.
Apply the concept to a small, fictional API scenario.
Review a communication design and justify appropriate choices.

understand.concept: Parsing determines whether input can be interpreted according to a format and produces a structured representation. Validation checks whether that representation meets an application's rules. A value can parse successfully and still be invalid—for example, a JSON age field may be a string, negative, or outside the allowed range.
understand.whyItMatters: Separating these steps produces clearer errors and avoids assuming that well-formed data is trustworthy or appropriate.
understand.analogy: Think of a delivery process with a sender, a message, and a receiver who returns a confirmation or explanation.
understand.analogyLimit: Software communication may involve complex protocols, asynchronous timing, security, and partial failures that this everyday analogy cannot fully capture.

explain.narrative:
Parsing determines whether input can be interpreted according to a format and produces a structured representation. Validation checks whether that representation meets an application's rules. A value can parse successfully and still be invalid—for example, a JSON age field may be a string, negative, or outside the allowed range.

Use the protocol and service documentation as the authoritative guide for a real API. Examples here are conceptual and intentionally do not make live network calls.

commonMistakes: Assuming every request succeeds or returns the same shape.
Treating parsing as validation or authentication as authorization.
Ignoring timeout, rate-limit, and failure responses.
Embedding secret credentials in public client code.
Retrying operations without considering duplicate side effects.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Take a JSON text containing a user record. Show the parse result, then check required fields, types, length limits, and allowed values. Include one syntactically valid but invalid record.

independentTask.instructions: Write a validation specification for an API payload. Separate parsing errors from validation errors and define expected messages for at least four invalid cases.
